newsitem.title: FRANCE: French spending decree to cover job subsidy reform.
newsitem.headline: French spending decree to cover job subsidy reform.

text.p: A government decree enshrining the minimum pay rise and other spending measures announced by French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin in June will also address the cost of reforming job subsidies, a government source said on Tuesday.

The decree, to be issued mid-July, will cover the "budgetary effects" of measures announced in Jospin's maiden parliamentary speech, namely a four percent minimum wage rise, housing aid upgrades, quadrupling of "back-to-school" payouts and the transition to a reformed employment subsidy system, the source said.
The measures will then be dealt with within the context of full budget decisions at the end of the year, the source said.
The rejig of job subsidies to promote youth employment will involve costs during the transition period from the old to the new system, the source said.
"The switch from one system to another has to be managed in financial terms and the decree will take account of the cost," said the source.
